name: Israel, the Chosen People
description: The people descended from Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, whom God chose as his own possession and bound to himself by covenant at Sinai, called also by the poetic name Jeshurun (Exod 19:5-6; Deut 7:6; Isa 44:2).

affected_links.basis: Haydock (Berthier on Ps 28:6): 'Jeshurun is a title of Israel... who was a figure of the Messias, the beloved of God'; verses Ps 28:6, Matt 2:15
affected_links.why: Berthier's figure is Israel itself under its title; Israel, God's chosen son, read of Christ (Hos 11:1; Matt 2:15) is unchanged. The description keeps the name Jeshurun.

affected_links.basis: Haydock (Witham on Rev 15:2): Israel delivered through the Red Sea figures the Christians
affected_links.why: Israel the people → the Church is exactly the Witham reading, and it is also what §§60, 751, 759, 762, 781 teach.

rejected_alternatives.option: name 'Israel, the Chosen People (Jeshurun)' (all six proposals)
rejected_alternatives.why: Same outcome, but the parenthetical is obscure to a general reader. Jeshurun is just a poetic name for Israel (Deut 32:15; 33:5; Isa 44:2), so it belongs in the description, not the name.

rejected_alternatives.option: new Type 'Israel, the Chosen People', keeping israel-jeshurun
rejected_alternatives.why: That would create two nodes for one people. Jeshurun is Israel.
No proposal touches that Type, and it sits on sensitive ground. It is listed under catalog_suggestions for the user to decide as its own item.

rationale: All six proposals (§§60, 751, 753, 759, 762, 781) agree on this. The catalog Type is Israel under a poetic title, so naming it for the people itself makes it cover the Catechism's 'chosen people' without a near-duplicate. The name is plain and positive, in the Catechism's own words (§60, §751), and the description is Scripture-first. The id stays israel-jeshurun. The Daughter of Zion is kept separate (td-020): she is a personified figure with Marian and ecclesial antitypes, not the people as such.

name: The Twelve Patriarchs and Tribes of Israel
description: The twelve sons of Jacob and the twelve tribes of Israel descended from and named after them (Gen 49:28).

affected_links.basis: Haydock (Menochius on Matt 10:1): the apostles 'correspond to the number of the Jewish patriarchs, by whom they may be said to have been prefigured'
affected_links.why: The patriarchs stay named first. Scripture uses the twelvefold figure both ways: the apostles judge 'the twelve tribes' (Matt 19:28), and the city's gates bear the tribes' names while its foundations bear the apostles' (Rev 21:12-14).

rejected_alternatives.option: new Type 'The Twelve Tribes of Israel'
rejected_alternatives.why: That would nearly duplicate this Type. Each tribe bears its patriarch's name, and Gen 49:28 calls the twelve sons 'the twelve tribes of Israel'. The figure is the number twelve, which tribes and patriarchs share.
That is Israel as a whole people. §765's point is the twelvefold structure that the Twelve 'represent'.

rationale: §765: the Twelve, 'representing the twelve tribes of Israel'. Broadening keeps one twelvefold figure instead of two near-twins (patriarchs vs tribes). This is not the founder-vs-institution blur that rule 1 guards against: Scripture itself treats the twelve sons and the twelve tribes as one twelvefold figure (Gen 49:28; Acts 7:8; Rev 21:12).

name: The Cloud of the Lord's Glory
description: The cloud in which the Lord's glory appeared to Israel: the pillar of cloud and fire that led them out of Egypt and through the wilderness, the cloud that covered Mount Sinai and the tent of meeting, and the cloud that filled Solomon's Temple (Exod 13:21-22; 24:15-18; 40:34-38; 1 Kgs 8:10-11).

affected_links.basis: CCC 1094 ('as did the cloud and the crossing of the Red Sea') + Haydock; verse Exod 13:22
affected_links.why: The description names the pillar that led Israel out of Egypt, the cloud of 1 Cor 10:1-2 ('all under the cloud... baptized into Moses in the cloud'). §697 itself cites 1 Cor 10:1-2 for this cloud.

affected_links.basis: Haydock (Ambrose, De Sacramentis 6): the fire of the pillar designates Christ; verse Exod 13:22
affected_links.why: The description keeps 'the pillar of cloud and fire'. §697 adds a second warrant for this pair: 'In the Holy Spirit, Christ fulfills these figures.'

affected_links.basis: Haydock (Ambrose): the cloud figures the Holy Spirit; verse Exod 13:22
affected_links.why: §697 makes the cloud in all its OT appearances an image of the Spirit, so the link is if anything strengthened.
Unchanged; the cloud of §1094 is the exodus cloud named in the description.

rejected_alternatives.option: two new Types, 'The Cloud on Mount Sinai' and 'The Cloud Filling Solomon's Temple' (as proposed)
rejected_alternatives.why: §697 treats 'the cloud' as one image showing itself in several theophanies (Sinai, the tent of meeting, the desert, the Temple). Its footnotes join the desert cloud (1 Cor 10:1-2; Exod 40:36), the Sinai cloud (Exod 24:15-18) and the tent cloud (Exod 33:9-10). Scripture also presents one continuous cloud of glory (Exod 13:21 → 19:9 → 24:16 → 40:34-38), and 1 Kgs 8:10-11 echoes Exod 40:34-35 word for word. Three nodes would each carry the same §697 quote to the same antitype.

rejected_alternatives.option: keep the name 'Cloud in the Desert' and only widen the description
rejected_alternatives.why: The name would then mislabel the Sinai and Temple rows.

rationale: After this broadening, the two §697 rows (Sinai, Solomon) duplicate the existing bucket-A row c697:cloud-in-desert>christ: same pair, same quote. Review should fold them into that one link. The id stays cloud-in-desert. Ezekiel's vision of the glory departing (the-glory-of-the-lord-departing-the-temple) is a different event and stays separate.

name: The Law of Moses (Old Covenant)
description: The Law the Lord gave Israel through Moses and the covenant he made with them at Sinai, sealed with the blood of sacrifice (Exod 24:7-8; Deut 5:2-3).

affected_links.basis: Haydock: 'the law and the prophets are fulfilled and verified in Jesus Christ'; verses Matt 17:6, Rom 3:31
affected_links.why: The Law is still named first; Christ fulfils the Law and the covenant alike.

affected_links.basis: Haydock (Witham on Heb 10:1): the law 'but a shadow of the good things to come'
affected_links.why: Heb 8:5 and 9:1-10 say the same of the first covenant's worship and sanctuary, so the shadow reading covers the broader Type.

affected_links.basis: Haydock: 'the gospel has perfected or fulfilled the law' (Matt 5:17); verses include Ezek 16:60, Bar 2:35, Heb 7:20
affected_links.why: The broader Type now mirrors its antitype's name: Law (Old Covenant) → Gospel (New Covenant). Several of the link's verses (Ezek 16:60; Bar 2:35) already speak of the covenant.

affected_links.basis: Haydock (Witham on Gal 4:22): Ishmael 'represent[s] that covenant of the former law delivered on Mount Sina'
affected_links.why: The note already says 'covenant ... delivered on Mount Sina', which is Gal 4:24 ('two covenants; one from Mount Sinai'). The new name fits Paul's allegory better than the old one.

rejected_alternatives.option: new Type 'The Old Covenant (Sinai Covenant)' (as proposed, 3 votes)
rejected_alternatives.why: That gives two near-synonymous OT nodes pointing at the same NT node (the-gospel-new-covenant). Scripture binds the Sinai covenant and its Law together: 'the book of the covenant... the blood of the covenant' (Exod 24:7-8); 'two covenants... one from Mount Sinai' (Gal 4:24); 'when they read the old covenant' (2 Cor 3:14). The Catechism does too: 'the covenant of Mount Sinai and, through Moses, ... his law' (§62); 'The gift of the commandments and of the Law is part of the covenant' (§2060). The catalog's NT side already joins Gospel and New Covenant in one Type.
'The Mosaic Law' is too narrow a label for 'the old Alliance' (§759) and 'the Old Covenant' (§778).

Equally neutral, but 'Old Covenant' is the term in all three quotes (§§759, 778, 781) and in Scripture (2 Cor 3:14), and the Catechism uses it positively (§121, 'never been revoked'). It is also the exact counterpart of the antitype's name.

rationale: §§759, 778, 781 name the Old Covenant as preparing for and figuring the New. The catalog's Mosaic Law Type is already used for this (Witham's 'covenant of the former law delivered on Mount Sina'). Broadening it, rather than creating a twin, keeps one OT node opposite 'The Gospel (New Covenant)'. ceremonial-law and dietary-laws remain separate, more precise subsets. The id stays the-mosaic-law. The proposers' worry about the → heaven link is answered above (Heb 8:5; 9:1-10).

name: The Creation of the World
description: God's creation of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them 'in the beginning', the work of six days completed on the seventh (Gen 1:1-2:3).

rejected_alternatives.why: That is the Catechism's term only when it is set against the new creation (§349). 'The Creation of the World' is what a general reader would say, and it pairs just as clearly with 'The New Creation in Christ'.
The sky of Ps 19 read of the Church's preachers: one created image, not the work of creation.
The first man, not the whole work of creation.

rejected_alternatives.option: fold in 'The Spirit over the Waters of Creation'
rejected_alternatives.why: The Easter Vigil (§1218) and §1224 single out Gen 1:2 as its own figure of Baptism. Folding it in would give 'creation → Baptism', which says less than the Catechism does.

rationale: 'First creation' (§§280, 281, 315, 349) and 'creation world' (§§759, 778) are the same figure under two names, so they become one Type. The §759/§778 rows are low-confidence (the sense may be temporal: 'from the beginning'), but that is for verification. The Type is needed for §§280/315/349 anyway.

name: The Spirit over the Waters of Creation
description: The Spirit of God moving over the face of the waters at the beginning of creation (Gen 1:2).

rejected_alternatives.why: The liturgy and the Catechism treat the Spirit-borne waters as a figure distinct from creation as a whole (§1218: 'your Spirit breathed on the waters, making them the wellspring of all holiness'; §1224). This mirrors the catalog's flood/ark distinction.
That Type collects the Exodus and wilderness water wonders. The Vigil blessing lists creation, flood, Red Sea and Jordan as separate figures.

rationale: Two rows: → baptism (§§1217-1218) and → The Baptism of Jesus (§1224). Both rest on Gen 1:2 specifically.

name: The New Creation in Christ
description: The renewal of all things, begun in Christ's Resurrection and in each believer made a new creature in Baptism, and to be completed in the new heavens and the new earth (2 Cor 5:17; Rev 21:1-5).

rejected_alternatives.why: §349: the Resurrection begins the new creation; it is the inaugurating event, not the renewed creation.
Those are the inheritance and the dwelling of the blessed; the new creation is cosmic ('new heavens and a new earth').
The person, not the renewal he works.

rationale: The Catechism's recurring counterpart of creation (§§280, 315, 349, 1224, 2174). It is a NT reality in its own right (2 Cor 5:17; Gal 6:15; Rev 21:5).
description_before_verifier: The renewal of all things begun in Christ's Resurrection and to be completed in the new heavens and the new earth (2 Cor 5:17; Rev 21:1-5).

name: The Sabbath
description: The seventh day, on which God rested from the work of creation and which he blessed and hallowed, given to Israel to keep holy as a sign of the covenant (Gen 2:2-3; Exod 20:8-11; 31:16-17).

rejected_alternatives.option: two Types: 'God's Seventh-Day Rest' (event) and 'The Sabbath' (institution)
rejected_alternatives.why: Here the tradition does not separate them. Scripture grounds the commandment in God's rest (Exod 20:11), and Heb 4:4-10 reads God's rest and the sabbath as one figure of the rest that remains. The Catechism uses 'sabbath' for both (§345 heading; §2169; §2172), and §2002's 'you rested on the seventh day... the sabbath of eternal life' is the same figure. Both antitypes (eternal rest; the Lord's Day) read true of one Type.
A distinct sabbatical institution (Lev 25) with its own link to Christ's redemption.
The sabbath is rooted in creation before Sinai (§§345-348, 2169) and is taught as its own sign (§2171). Folding it into the Law would bury the clearest single figure the Catechism treats at length.

rationale: One Type for 10 rows (§§314, 349, 2002, 2169-2176, 2190). The description stays plain and Scripture-first. It does not carry the 'replaced' wording of §2175/§2190, which belongs to the rows' quotes, not to the node.

name: The Lord's Day (Sunday)
description: The first day of the week, the day of Christ's Resurrection, on which Christians gather for the breaking of bread (Acts 20:7; Rev 1:10).

rejected_alternatives.why: The event the day commemorates; §§2174-2176 make the day itself the fulfilment of the sabbath.
The sacrament celebrated on Sunday (§2177), not the day.
Sunday 'symbolizes' and 'recalls' the new creation (§§2174, 2190); the sign and what it signifies are distinct.

rationale: Same name as the held nt-figure row c2175 (Lord's Day → eternal-life), so the later phase reuses this id automatically.
held_alignment: c2175:new:lord day sunday>eternal-life (same group key, resolves to the-lords-day)

name: Abraham
description: The patriarch whom God called out of his own country and promised to make the father of a great people, in whom all the families of the earth would be blessed (Gen 12:1-3).

rejected_alternatives.option: one Type 'Abraham' that also carries the Mamre row
rejected_alternatives.why: §2571 makes the hospitality at Mamre the figure ('foreshadows the annunciation'), an event-to-event parallel. The catalog already separates isaac from binding-of-isaac, and Abraham should follow the same precedent.

§762's figure is Abraham as the father of a great people, which prepares the gathering of the People of God (cf. Rom 4:16-17, 'the father of us all'). That is a person-level figure, parallel to the people-level Israel row in the same paragraph. A person node is also the one later work will reuse (e.g. §2676, Abraham's faith and Mary's).
A different person, or a different event.

rationale: The catalog has Sarah, Isaac and Jacob but no Abraham. The held prophecy rows proposing 'The Promise to Abraham' (§§422, 706) make a different kind of claim, an oracle fulfilled in Christ. They are not clearly the same figure, so no name is forced on them. If the later phase wants a node, `abraham` is available, but only with care, since prophecy is not typology.

name: Abraham's Hospitality at Mamre
description: Abraham's welcome of three visitors at the oaks of Mamre, who announced that Sarah would bear him a son (Gen 18:1-15).

rejected_alternatives.why: That would blur an event with a person (rule 1). The Catechism's figure is the visit and its announcement.
Sarah's links (→ mary, → the-one-true-church) are person-level, and the figure here is the announcing visit.

rationale: Gold paragraph §2571: 'Abraham's remarkable hospitality at Mamre foreshadows the annunciation of the true Son of the promise.' The name is in the Catechism's own words.

name: The Annunciation
description: The angel Gabriel's announcement to the Virgin Mary that she would conceive and bear a son, Jesus, the Son of the Most High (Luke 1:26-38).

rejected_alternatives.why: The Son announced; the antitype in §2571 is the announcing event, matched to the announcement at Mamre.
The person; the paragraph's stress is on the announced Son of the promise.

rationale: Needed as the event-level antitype of §2571. It will also serve §697's cloud overshadowing Mary (Luke 1:35) if that is ever drawn at event level.

name: The Baptism of Jesus
description: Jesus' baptism by John in the Jordan, when the Spirit descended on him like a dove and the Father declared him his beloved Son (Matt 3:13-17).

rejected_alternatives.why: The sacrament. §1224 and §701 speak of Jesus' own baptism by John, which the Catechism distinguishes from it.
The person, not this event.

rationale: Two reviewable rows (§701, §1224). The name matches the held nt-figure rows (§§536, 556), which resolve to this id automatically.
held_alignment: c536 / c556 'The Baptism of Jesus' (same group key)

name: The Temptation of Jesus in the Desert
description: Jesus' forty days of fasting in the desert, where he was tempted by Satan and remained obedient to the Father (Matt 4:1-11).

rejected_alternatives.why: The Paschal victory; §539 says the desert victory 'anticipates' it, so the two are distinct.
§539 matches Israel's forty years to Jesus' forty days, event to event.

rejected_alternatives.option: name 'The Temptation of Christ in the Desert'
rejected_alternatives.why: Changed to 'Jesus' to match its neighbour 'The Baptism of Jesus' (Gospel events of his life); same figure.

rationale: §539: 'in contrast to those who had once provoked God during forty years in the desert'. §538 calls the temptations a recapitulation of Israel's in the desert.

name: The Transfiguration
description: Christ's transfiguration on the mountain before Peter, James and John, when Moses and Elijah appeared talking with him and a voice spoke from the cloud (Matt 17:1-8).
depends: c2583:new:lord passing by at horeb cleft rock>new:transfiguration

rejected_alternatives.why: A different glorification event.
§2583 names 'the mountain of the Transfiguration', the event.

rationale: Matches the held nt-figure row §556 ('The Transfiguration'), which resolves here automatically.

name: Confirmation
description: The sacrament in which the baptized are sealed with the gift of the Holy Spirit through the laying on of hands and anointing with chrism, as the apostles laid hands on the baptized in Samaria (Acts 8:14-17).

rejected_alternatives.why: Generic. Both rows name Confirmation, and the catalog already holds the specific sacraments (Baptism, Eucharist, Holy Orders, Penance).
The event Confirmation 'perpetuates' (§1288), not the sacrament.

rationale: This closes the gap that started the pass (the NT column held 4 of 7 sacraments). Both dependent rows are synthesized (§1150 + §1288 low; §1150 + §1294 medium), so the Type only lands if a row survives verification.

name: Matrimony
description: The sacrament by which a baptized man and woman are joined in a lifelong covenant of marriage that signifies the union of Christ and the Church (Eph 5:25-32).
depends: c1642:new:nuptial covenant god and israel>new:matrimony sacrament marriage

rejected_alternatives.why: Redundant. 'Matrimony' matches the catalog's plain sacrament names (Baptism, Eucharist, Holy Orders).
What marriage signifies, not the sacrament (§1617).
The OT marriage of the first couple.
Generic; §1642 names Matrimony.

rationale: One reviewable row (§1642). The held nt-figure rows §§1617, 1659, 1661 share the group key and resolve here.
held_alignment: c1617 / c1659 / c1661 'Matrimony (Sacrament of Marriage)' (same group key)
c2384 'Matrimony (Sacramental Marriage)': different key, map to matrimony by hand in the later phase

name: Laying On of Hands (Old Testament)
description: The Old Testament gesture of laying hands on a person or an offering to bless, consecrate or commission, as when Moses laid his hands on Joshua (Num 27:18-23).

rejected_alternatives.why: A different rite, listed separately in §1150's own sentence.
An institution; the gesture also blessed and commissioned non-priests (Num 27:23; Gen 48:14).
Same figure. 'Old Testament' follows the catalog's ot-priesthood / ot-sacrifices, and the marker keeps the name free for the NT gesture (Acts 8:17; 1 Tim 4:14).

rationale: §1150 lists it among the OT 'liturgical signs' the Church sees as 'a prefiguring of the sacraments of the New Covenant'.

name: The Seventy Elders
description: The seventy elders of Israel on whom the Lord placed some of the spirit that was on Moses, so that they might bear the burden of the people with him (Num 11:16-17, 24-25).

rejected_alternatives.option: broaden ot-priesthood to cover the elders
rejected_alternatives.why: It fails the link test: ot-priesthood → christ-high-priest does not read true of the elders, who were not priests. §1541 also lists them apart from Aaron and the Levites.
The man whose spirit was shared, not the seventy who received it.

rationale: Gold paragraph §1541 names 'the institution of the seventy elders' as a prefiguring of the ordained ministry. §1542 is the ordination prayer that recalls it.

name: The Daughter of Zion
description: Zion, that is Jerusalem and the people of God, personified by the prophets as a daughter called to rejoice because the Lord her king comes to dwell in her midst (Zeph 3:14-17; Zech 9:9).

rejected_alternatives.option: use_existing israel-jeshurun (Israel, the Chosen People, td-001)
rejected_alternatives.why: She is a personification of the people, but the Catechism uses her as a figure in her own right. She is 'a figure of his Church' (§559), and Mary is 'the daughter of Zion in person' (§2676; §489, §722). 'Israel → Mary' would not read true; 'the Daughter of Zion → Mary' does.
The jewelled city of Tob 13 / Isa 54 (→ glorified Church), a specific vision.
The remnant of Zeph 3:12-13 precedes the oracle but is a different figure.
A different personification and text.

rationale: Three rows (§559 → Church; §722, §2676 → Mary). The description is plain and Scripture-first, built on the prophets' call to rejoice.

name: God's Marriage Covenant with Israel
description: The covenant between the Lord and his people Israel, which the prophets portray as a marriage of faithful love, with the Lord as husband and Israel as his bride (Isa 54:5; Jer 2:2; Hos 2:19-20).
depends: c1642:new:nuptial covenant god and israel>new:matrimony sacrament marriage

rejected_alternatives.option: names 'The Nuptial Covenant of God and Israel' / 'Israel, Bride of the Lord (Nuptial Covenant)'
rejected_alternatives.why: Same figure. 'Marriage' is the plainer word, and the name keeps the stress on God's covenant rather than on Israel's conduct. The catalog already has gods-healing-word and gods-wonders-by-water in this form.
§1611 names the prophets' covenant image and the Song of Solomon as separate witnesses. The Canticle's bride is read of the Church and the soul; the prophets' bride is Israel under covenant.
The people, not the spousal bond. The bride's antitype is the Church, so that Type's → christ link would blur.
The prophet whose marriage enacts the image, not the covenant itself.

rationale: The two proposals are one figure (§§796, 1611, 1612, 1642), so they become one Type. The description keeps to what the Catechism says the prophets saw: 'exclusive and faithful married love' (§1611).

name: Wisdom Personified
description: Wisdom personified as a woman who calls aloud to the simple and who was beside God when he made the world (Prov 8:1-31).

rejected_alternatives.why: The parenthetical is narrower than §721's 'texts on wisdom'. The verse reference sits in the description.
The wise king, not personified Wisdom.

rationale: §721 (footnote Prov 8:1-9): the Tradition reads the wisdom texts 'in relation to Mary', the Seat of Wisdom. The name is deliberately not Marian, because the same figure is read of Christ (1 Cor 1:24) and may gain that link later.

name: Eve Formed from Adam's Side
description: God casting a deep sleep on Adam and forming the woman from a rib taken from his side (Gen 2:21-22).

rejected_alternatives.why: The person (→ Mary as the first mother). §766's parallel is the event of her formation.

rejected_alternatives.option: broaden adam-and-eve (Marriage of Adam and Eve)
rejected_alternatives.why: Its one link (→ christ-church, Eph 5:31-32) would survive. But the tradition treats the Church born from the side of the sleeping Christ (John 19:34) as its own figure, distinct from the nuptial union, and the antitypes differ (the Church born vs Christ united to the Church).

rationale: §766: 'As Eve was formed from the sleeping Adam's side, so the Church was born from the pierced heart of Christ.'

name: Elijah's Sacrifice on Mount Carmel
description: The sacrifice on Mount Carmel, consumed by fire from heaven in answer to Elijah's prayer at the hour of the evening offering (1 Kgs 18:36-39).

new_groups: fire from heaven on mount carmel

rejected_alternatives.option: two Types: 'Fire from Heaven on Mount Carmel' and 'Elijah's Sacrifice on Mount Carmel'
rejected_alternatives.why: One event (1 Kgs 18:36-39). §2583 cross-references §696, and both rows rest on the fire falling on the sacrifice at the prophet's prayer.

rejected_alternatives.option: name 'Fire from Heaven on Mount Carmel'
rejected_alternatives.why: That fits the Pentecost link but reads oddly against the Eucharistic epiclesis. The event name covers both, and the description puts the fire first.
elijah → eucharist rests on the bread of 1 Kgs 19:8 (Haydock), not on Carmel. Mapping here would blur a person with an event and merge two different Eucharistic figures.
The poetic lightning of Ps 29, a different text and figure.

rationale: Gold paragraph §696 calls 'this event' a figure of the Spirit's fire. §2583 links the Carmel plea to the epiclesis.

name: The Lord Passing By at Horeb
description: The Lord's passing by on Mount Horeb, when Moses, sheltered in a cleft of the rock, saw his back but not his face, and when Elijah, at the mouth of a cave, heard him in a still small voice (Exod 33:18-23; 1 Kgs 19:9-13).

new_groups: lord passing by at horeb cleft rock

depends: c2583:new:lord passing by at horeb cleft rock>new:transfiguration

rejected_alternatives.option: name 'The Lord Passing By at Horeb (the Cleft of the Rock)'
rejected_alternatives.why: Shortened. The cleft belongs in the description.
Persons. The figure is the theophany, which §2583 explicitly joins for both men.
A different Horeb theophany (Exod 3).

rejected_alternatives.option: broaden cloud-in-desert (The Cloud of the Lord's Glory, td-003)
rejected_alternatives.why: No cloud at the cleft. The figure is the veiled vision of God's face.

rationale: §2583 joins the two Horeb theophanies ('Elijah, like Moses before him, hides "in a cleft of the rock"') and completes them on the mountain of the Transfiguration. One Type for one pattern.

name: The Mercy Seat
description: The golden cover of the ark of the covenant (called the propitiatory in the Douay-Rheims), between the cherubim, where the Lord promised to meet Moses and on which the high priest sprinkled the blood of atonement (Exod 25:17-22; Lev 16:14-15).

rejected_alternatives.why: The ark is read as God's dwelling (→ heaven, → Mary, 'the place where the glory of the Lord dwells', §2676). §433's figure is the propitiatory cover and the atonement made on it, the hilasterion of Rom 3:25 and Heb 9:5, which the tradition reads specifically of Christ the expiation.
The sanctuary room (→ ascension, heaven).
A different Day-of-Atonement rite.

rationale: §433 cites Exod 25:22, Lev 16:15, Rom 3:25 and Heb 9:5. It joins the Day-of-Atonement family as its most precise member.
description_before_verifier: The golden cover of the ark of the covenant, between the cherubim, where the Lord promised to meet Moses and on which the high priest sprinkled the blood of atonement (Exod 25:17-22; Lev 16:14-15).

name: Israel's Forty Years of Testing in the Wilderness
description: The forty years in which the Lord led Israel, his son, through the wilderness, humbling and testing it and feeding it with manna, that it might learn that man does not live by bread alone (Deut 8:2-3).
rationale: Proposed by the verifier (Fr. Augustine) on c539: what §539 says Jesus fulfills is Israel's forty years of testing as God's son (§538: the temptations 'recapitulate ... the temptations of Israel in the desert'); its disobedience is only the contrast. The existing israels-disobedience-in-the-wilderness Type is the 1 Cor 10 warning figure (→ final-judgment) and is kept distinct. Approved by the user 2026-10-20.
